newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian right attacks government in mass rally.
newsitem.headline: Italian right attacks government in mass rally.

text.p: More than 100,000 supporters of Italy's main opposition centre-right bloc packed the cathedral square in central Milan at the weekend in an anti-government rally one week before run-offs in key mayoral elections.

"A coalition of powers is increasingly threatening our well-being, our democracy, our future and the freedom of our children," centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi told cheering crowds at the demonstration on Saturday .
"(The centre-left governent) is a regime disguised in white gloves...It is a left impregnated with ideology, with communism," he said.

Berlusconi has stepped up his attacks on the government since centre-right candidates took the lead in mayoral elections in the prize northern cities of Milan and Turin in the first round of voting last week. Run-offs will be held on May 11.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for a majority in parliament but has a testy relationship with the party which has opposed several of its initiatives on ideological grounds.
Berlusconi said the centre-right was starting "the long march towards the reconquest of the country".

Supporters whistled when Berlusconi's ally, hard-right leader Gianfranco Fini, attacked President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro. Fini said the president, who has stepped into political debates on Europe recently, was "the real head of the ruling coalition".

Prodi has pushed through tough budgets and tax increases to try to win Italy a place in the first wave of monetary union but Berlusconi said Italians were being crippled and banners at the demonstration called for "less taxes, more jobs".
